title: Is a head transplant really a thing?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the proposed human head transplant (more accurately a whole-body transplant) championed by Italian surgeon Sergio Canavero, who planned to attempt it with Russian computer engineer Valery Spiridonov, who has Werdnig-Hoffmann disease. They cover the history of animal head transplants (Demikhov's dog experiments, Robert White's 1970 monkey head transplant in Cleveland), the scientific criticism from the medical community, Wren's mouse spinal cord work in China, the proposed surgical procedure (therapeutic hypothermia, color-coded reattachment, PEG glue, Texas nanostructure scaffolds, medically induced coma), ethical and psychological concerns, funding problems, and the "yuck factor." The episode ends with a listener mail segment from John Patrick Vitti about the show's anniversary.

segments.title: Introduction to head transplant debate
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the topic of human head transplants, note the controversy in the medical community, and mention Sergio Canavero's plan to attempt the surgery with Valery Spiridonov, who has Werdnig-Hoffmann disease.

segments.title: History of animal head transplants
segments.summary: Discussion of Vladimir Demikhov's dog experiments with grafted heads and legs, and Robert White's 1970 monkey head transplant in Cleveland, including the unconnected spinal cord and critics' accounts of the experiment.

segments.title: Canavero's critics and mouse research
segments.summary: The hosts describe recent mouse spinal cord studies in China and South Korea, scientists' skepticism, Ren Xiaoping's call to slow down, and Canavero's brash public style and funding claims.

segments.title: Canavero's 2013 proposed procedure and survival odds
segments.summary: Overview of Canavero's 2013 paper in Surgical Neurology International, the survival rates in rat studies, and the claimed nine percent chance of a normal life that doctors dispute.

segments.title: Step-by-step surgical plan
segments.summary: The hosts walk through the proposed procedure: cooling both patients with therapeutic hypothermia, a one-hour time window, color-coding muscles, precise spinal cord severing, PEG glue fusion, the Texas peg graphene nanospiral scaffold, and electrical stimulation.
topics: PEG polyethylene glycol spinal cord repair

segments.title: Recovery, ethics, and psychological concerns
segments.summary: Discussion of the planned medically induced coma, the recovery goals, psychological identity concerns, ethical questions about gender change and wealthy patients, and the rejection risk.

segments.title: Funding, animal ethics, and the yuck factor
segments.summary: Canavero's funding efforts, Russian government refusal, the ethics of animal experiments, and the concept of the yuck factor and folk biology.

segments.title: Listener mail: podcast anniversary
segments.summary: Listener John Patrick Vitti writes about how the show has influenced him over four years and mentions the hosts' Tuesday and Thursday schedule.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank the listener and give contact information and the website.
